name: Concha y Toro Cabernet Sauvignon Don Melchor 2017
text:
## Concha y Toro Cabernet Sauvignon Don Melchor 2017

**The story.** Don Melchor de Concha y Toro, a visionary 19th-century grower, planted vines brought from [Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux_wine) at Pirque, at the foot of the [Andes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andes), built his family's summer house there and laid the foundations of [Concha y Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concha_y_Toro) ([Don Melchor](https://donmelchor.com/story/), in Spanish). A century later, the great French oenologist [Émile Peynaud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89mile_Peynaud), "the father of modern winemaking", tasted Cabernet Sauvignon from [Puente Alto](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Vi%C3%B1a+Don+Melchor,+Puente+Alto,+Chile&t=k) in the [Maipo Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maipo_Province) and recognised the terroir. He suggested his closest collaborator, Jacques Boissenot, adviser to famous Bordeaux châteaux, to lead the project; Jacques worked on it until 2013, when his son Eric took over, with winemaker Enrique Tirado ([Don Melchor](https://donmelchor.com/story/)).

Don Melchor was the first Chilean wine to show the world that Chile could make great wine: with its second vintage, 1988, it became the first Chilean wine ranked among the world's best by Wine Spectator ([Don Melchor](https://donmelchor.com/story/)). The vineyard sits more than 2,000 feet up at the foot of the Andes, with Cabernet vines over 30 years old descended from pre-[phylloxera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylloxera) Bordeaux selections brought in the late 19th century ([Total Wine](https://concierge.totalwine.com/concierge-offers/don-melchor-library-release-maipo-valley-chile)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Chile vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/chile) says that after severe fires across large areas of southern Chile early in 2017, the harvest started early, and the generally warm year gave ripe fruit that can be jammy in some reds. Don Melchor's altitude kept it fresh: Total Wine's tasters found "a wonderful mineral weight that speaks directly to its Andean origins".

**What the critics say for 2017.**
- **[James Suckling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Suckling): 99**, as quoted by [Total Wine](https://concierge.totalwine.com/concierge-offers/don-melchor-library-release-maipo-valley-chile). "Perhaps the greatest Don Melchor ever made", with "fantastic aromas of blackcurrants and other dark fruit with crushed stone, iron and oysters" and "incredible energy and depth".
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 93.1** (from your CellarTracker list).
- (Wine Advocate and Wine Spectator notes exist on retail pages I couldn't read in full, so I've left them out.)

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is nine years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2021 to 2027. So it is in its prime: blackcurrant, crushed stone, iron, cedar and a mineral backbone, with years in hand if well stored. Decant an hour ahead and serve at 17 to 18°C.

**Food.** Total Wine suggests hearty meats: an Argentine [asado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asado), Peruvian [anticuchos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anticucho) or Korean [galbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galbi), or aged Manchego and Parmigiano with more austere vintages ([Total Wine](https://concierge.totalwine.com/concierge-offers/don-melchor-library-release-maipo-valley-chile)).

**Value and where to buy.** Don Melchor is easy to find here: ZYN has the 2020 ($197), 2021 ($241) and 2022 ($210); BSW Liquor has the 2022 at $185; BC Liquor lists Don Melchor at $225.99.

**From the history books**
- **The first Chilean wine among the world's best.** Don Melchor's 1988, only its second vintage, was the first Chilean wine ranked among the world's best by Wine Spectator, a landmark for Chilean wine ([Don Melchor](https://donmelchor.com/story/)).
- **Peynaud's verdict.** It took a French master, Émile Peynaud, to recognise Puente Alto's potential at a time when fine Chilean wine was still in its infancy ([Don Melchor](https://donmelchor.com/story/)).

**Curious details**
- **The devil's cellar.** In the late 1880s, according to Wine Enthusiast as quoted by Total Wine, Don Melchor's cellar was repeatedly raided by thieves, so he spread a rumour that his wines were guarded by the devil ([Total Wine](https://concierge.totalwine.com/concierge-offers/don-melchor-library-release-maipo-valley-chile)).
- **A Bordeaux family.** Jacques and Eric Boissenot are among Bordeaux's most famous consultants; father and son have guided Don Melchor since its first vintage ([Don Melchor](https://donmelchor.com/story/)).
